Situational awareness is # 1; the best way to avoid trouble is to avoid getting into situations where you can be trapped or attacked. Keep your head up and look around you when you're walking; don't wear headphones and don't get engrossed in texting. Whenever possible travel with a friend or friends, rather than by yourself.

I don't care how much self defense you know or how many pepper spray bottles you carry; if the guy -- or guys -- catches you unprepared then you are in trouble.

Martial arts training is helpful because it can give you an air of physical competence that makes it less likely for someone to attempt to intimidate you. But it takes natural talent and years of training to react without having to think about it. I'm all for learning how to fight but even the best black belt will tell you that your first option should always be to run.

[edit] Everyone thinks they're tough... until they get punched in the nose. Your eyes water, you panic and your heart races, and you want to cry. It's something you need to experience more than once before you can even begin to start thinking about being able to defend yourself in the event of a physical attack. Attackers are bullies and they will always pick someone they feel they can dominate easily, then they will strike hard and fast because this usually takes the fight out of the victim.

A lot of sexual assaults by strangers are crimes of opportunity so if you make it as difficult for them as possible it can frequently deter them from following through. Always run if you can, if you are trapped or somehow otherwise unable to get away, scream and make as much noise as possible. Bang on things if you can. Claw at their eyes, try to strike them in the groin, kick, do whatever it takes. A lot of times during a sexual assault someone becomes so terrified they simply freeze up and don't act. You want to make sure this doesn't happen to you.
